description: A Collection of application ideas which can be used to improve your coding skills.

summary.one_liner: A curated list of about 100 application project ideas, tiered from beginner to advanced, meant to give developers something concrete to build for practice.
summary.what_it_does: This is a link-and-description collection rather than code, organized into three tables by difficulty: Tier-1 Beginner, Tier-2 Intermediate, and Tier-3 Advanced. Each table lists a project name and a one-line description, such as a Pomodoro Clock, Markdown Previewer, Password Generator, or Discord Battleship bot. The README says each project is meant to come with an objective, user stories, optional bonus features, and resource links, though those per-project details are not in this README itself. It also points to a separate #100Days100Projects challenge with 100 smaller project ideas. Contributions are accepted through issues labeled "new idea" or pull requests.
use_cases: Find a project to build when you don't know what to code next
Practice JavaScript and front-end skills with small apps
Pick portfolio projects to show employers or clients
Find example ideas for coding tutorials or videos
notable: Projects are tiered by skill level in three tables (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced)
Describes each idea with an objective, user stories, and optional bonus features, according to the README
Includes a separate 100Days100Projects challenge with 100 smaller ideas
Open to community contributions via issues labeled 'new idea' or pull requests
caveats: Lists ideas only; the README does not provide implementation code for the projects
The README mentions a planned website for browsing projects, which is not yet available according to the text
Per-project details live in linked resources rather than in this README
